verdict.rationale: Epic's license grants access to the engine source code, and the docs cover running headless dedicated servers on your own infrastructure, so users can build and run the core product themselves. However, a probe shows source access is gated behind an account and EULA (the public GitHub API returns Not Found), and nothing in the evidence documents a standalone, self-managed install of the editor or toolchain. missing for 10: an ungated or openly licensed way to obtain the source, explicit docs on self-hosted or offline installation of the editor and engine, and independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Set up and run a dedicated server for your project.
